provenance: Synthetic example written by Claude for development. The reference marks are Claude's, not a teacher's. Replace with teacher-marked work before quoting agreement figures.
title: Cells and photosynthesis
subject: Science
schemeText:
Q1 Name the part of a plant cell where photosynthesis happens. (1) Chloroplast.
Q2 Write the word equation for photosynthesis. (2) carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen. 1 mark for correct reactants, 1 for correct products.
Q3 Name two structures found in plant cells but not animal cells. (2) Any two of: cell wall, chloroplast, permanent vacuole.
Q4 Why do plants need light for photosynthesis? (1) Light provides the energy for the reaction.
Q5 Suggest why a plant kept in the dark loses mass. (2) No photosynthesis so no glucose made (1); glucose still used in respiration (1).
pupilWork:
Q1 chloroplasts
Q2 carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen
Q3 a cell wall and a big vacuole
Q4 the light gives the energy that is needed to make glucose
Q5 in the dark it can't photosynthesise so no glucose is made, but it still respires and uses up the glucose it already had

reference.notes: Full marks. 'Big vacuole' accepted for permanent vacuole.

demoResult.feedback: You explained why the plant loses mass very clearly, linking photosynthesis and respiration. Next, practise writing the balanced symbol equation as well as the word equation.

criteria.evidence: a cell wall and a big vacuole
